devices.description: 12 x 400G QSFP-DD, 24 x 100G QSFP28 and 4 x 10G SFP+ 2RU aggregation router on a Broadcom Jericho2c+ with an Intel Xeon D Ice Lake and an OpenBMC service processor, sold as the AGR560 and stamped AS9947-36XKB. ALL PORTS ARE ON THE FRONT, NUMBERED FROM ZERO, in stacked pairs legended `N (up) (down) N+1`: the SFP+ quad at the left, three QSFP28 blocks of two columns by four rows, then three QSFP-DD blocks of two columns by two rows. THE SFP+ QUAD AND QSFP28 PORTS 0-3 ARE A COMBO PAIR and the panel says so with one continuous pink band across both. The out-of-band cluster carries MGMT, CONSOLE and ToD RJ-45s, 1PPS and 10 MHz coaxial timing jacks, a vertical USB 3.0 Type-A, a reset pinhole and FIVE system lamps - five, not the AIS800 family's six, because this machine has no ALRM. Two 2000 W Lite-On supplies and four fan trays are on the rear. It shares the AIS800-64D and AIS800-64O's 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell and their fan tray, and NOTHING ELSE: its supplies are half the power on different connectors and its port wall is a different machine entirely.

gaps.wanted: WHAT THE DC TERMINAL ACTUALLY IS. The datasheet names it and stops - "DC Inlet: Amphenol Terminal" - with no series, no part number and no drawing, and the guide adds only the wire gauge. So edgecore/agr560-psu-dc@1's block is drawn to the guide's rear elevation at 5.08 px/mm and nothing else: a 18.7 x 31.6 frame with two 10.7 wells on a 13.7 mm stud pitch. THE COUNT IS SAFE - the ordering table's cable is "6AWG PSU to 2 x Ring Terminal", so two studs is stated, not deduced - but the well diameter and the stud size are a round half of a measurement taken to about a quarter of a millimetre. An Amphenol catalogue drawing would replace them outright. The same gap is open on edgecore/ais800-64-psu-dc@1 for the same vendor's six-stud block.

A PHOTOGRAPH THAT SHOWS A SUPPLY LATCH ON THIS MACHINE AT ALL, in either build. Both supplies are drawn with a neutral #3d3d3f tab, and that is a measurement rather than a default: counted over the whole supply column of the datasheet's rear photograph at 9.56 px/mm, the AC build carries 133 red pixels - a 1.2 mm streak that is the red wire behind the fan guard - against the fan trays' 106,257 on the same face, and the module's right margin reads a flat dark grey. The guide's rear elevation, which is the only document that draws the DC build, cannot help: it renders both supplies with ZERO saturated pixels while colouring the trays' handles on the same drawing. SO THE HONEST READING IS THAT THE TAB IS NOT A COLOURED PART, and the AIS800 family's airflow-colour convention is not evidence here - that family ships in two airflows and photographs both, and this machine ships front-to-back only. Both components were first written with that family's red and green and both were corrected. What would close this is one clear photograph of either supply's right edge out of the chassis.

THE PERFORATION PATTERNS, PITCHES AND EXTENTS, which are the softest numbers on this face. The panel carries two styles - honeycomb along the top and bottom of the port wall and at the right-hand corners, and short slots above and below each QSFP-DD block - and both were found by clustering a local-variance map of a textured photograph rather than measured. The field RECTANGLES are good to about a millimetre; the pitches are estimates chosen to look right at 5 px/mm and are not read off anything. They are drawn because a panel with blank metal where perforation is would be wrong in a more misleading way than one whose hole pitch is approximate, but nothing here should be treated as measured. A mechanical drawing, or a photograph at 15 px/mm, closes it.

devices.description: 32 x 800G OSFP800 AI and data centre 1RU switch on a Broadcom Tomahawk 5 with an Intel Xeon D-1713NTE and an OpenBMC service processor, sold as the AIS800-32O. All ports are on the FRONT with two 25G SFP28 in-band management cages, an RJ-45 management jack, an RJ-45 console, a USB-C storage port, six system lamps and a reset button; two 2400 W supplies and SEVEN fan trays are on the rear. Its twin edgecore/ais800-32d is the same chassis, the same rear and the same management cluster with a QSFP-DD800 wall in place of this one's OSFP800 wall - and the two walls are laid out differently, which is the whole reason they are two models.

gaps.wanted: Which end of the rear the fan trays number from. The chassis silkscreens a mark on the rail beside each bay, and at the source's real resolution it cannot be read: the rear elevation is embedded in the PDF at 1.83 px/mm, where a 2 mm numeral is 3.7 pixels. Upscaling the page render to 600 dpi makes the marks LOOK legible - a "7" appeared convincingly on the rail at the right-hand end - but the same detector run on the embedded image at native resolution shows there is nothing there to read, so it was discarded. IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE FAMILY IS NOT CONSISTENT. edgecore/exp100-32x and edgecore/dcs240 both number their trays RIGHT to LEFT. The bays here carry rel-pos 1 to 7 LEFT to right because a view has to order them somehow, and NO numeral is silkscreened, because drawing one would assert what was not read. A photograph of the rear at 5 px/mm or better, or any figure that labels a tray, settles it in one look.

What the lamp on each fan tray means. Every one of the seven trays carries a round lens at its top left - a bright dome in a dark rim, about 3.4 mm across - and neither staged document mentions it. THE DC SUPPLY CARRIES ONE TOO, at the right of its lattice, 12 mm below its stowed bail where no part of the bail is; it was removed for a round on the AC sibling's reasoning and the reviewer caught it. THE AC SUPPLY CARRIES NONE: its matching ring sits exactly at the deployed bail's root and is the bail's end seen in perspective. The trays' lens sits where no bail is. The quick start guide's System LEDs/Buttons page lists the six chassis lamps and the RJ-45's pair and stops; the datasheet names port, management-port and system LEDs and no module lamp. The lamps are drawn because they are there, with the library's default off/on states. No green/amber legend is invented for them.

Where this face's port lamps are. The guide names them - "OSFP800 LEDs: Yellow (800G), Blue (400G), White (200G), Green (100G)" - so every port has at least one, and this elevation resolves none. The twin edgecore/ais800-32d puts four round windows in the 5.2 mm post beside each cage; an OSFP wall has only 0.3 mm between neighbouring cages, so whatever this model does it does somewhere else, and the drawing does not show where. No lamp is placed rather than one being guessed at. A photograph at 5 px/mm or better, or a port-LED figure, settles it.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Between them the two staged documents draw two elevations, a LED enlargement, two FRU figures, the airflow figures and a power-connection page, and not one of them shows a third face. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.

gaps.wanted: What the lamp on each fan tray means. Every one of the four trays carries a round lens at its top left - a bright dot about 2 mm across on the datasheet's rear photograph - and neither staged document mentions it. The quick start guide's System LEDs/Buttons page lists the six chassis lamps and the RJ-45's pair and stops; the datasheet names port, management-port and system LEDs and no module lamp. THE SUPPLIES CARRY NONE: the only round features on the AC supply's face are the two Phillips screw heads at its corners, which is the AIS800-32D's finding for the same vendor's supplies. Whether the port lamp's four colours are the only states it has. What the DC supply's six-bore input connector actually is. The guide's Connect Power page draws the face and legends the poles - "1. -48 - -60 VDC, 2. DC return, 3. Signal +, 4. datasheet.title: Edgecore COR550 (AS7926-40XKFB) Core Router data sheet

devices.description: 40x 100G QSFP28 and 13x 400G QSFP-DD 2RU cell-based core router (vendor alias AS7926-40XKFB), Broadcom BCM88690 Jericho2 with a BCM16K external TCAM and an Intel Xeon D-1548, ONIE-preloaded. Every port is on the front, along with a carrier-grade air filter that covers most of the faceplate that is not a cage; two AC supplies stack in one column at the left of the rear and five 4+1 fan trays fill the rest of it, front-to-back only.

gaps.wanted: WHICH OF A QSFP28 PORT'S THREE LAMPS SHOWS WHICH BREAKOUT LANE. The quick start guide's Status LEDs panel states colours by SPEED and not by lamp - 'QSFP28 Port LEDs: Blue - 100G, Yellow - 40G, Cyan - 2 x 50G, Magenta - 4 x 25G, Green - 4 x 10G' - and never says how many lamps a port has, let alone what each one means. The face draws three, and a 4 x 25G or 4 x 10G breakout has four lanes, so the obvious one-lamp-per-lane reading cannot be right. The lamps carry the library's off/on default and no legend is invented. A LED table naming the lamps, or a bench photograph of one port under a known breakout, settles it.

WHICH FABRIC PORT EACH LAMP OF A BLOCK'S TWO-LAMP COLUMN BELONGS TO. Each fabric block carries a vertical pair of lamps at its inboard edge, one pair per row, serving that row's two ports. Nothing in either document says which lamp is which port, and at 2.27 px/mm the lamps are 2 px across with no legend beside them. Each pair is therefore drawn `for:` BOTH of its ports rather than one lamp being assigned to each, because assigning them would be a guess wearing a measurement's clothes. A photograph of the fabric block at 5+ px/mm settles it.

THE OUTLINE OF EACH AIR-FILTER COVER AND THE POSITIONS OF ITS CAPTIVE SCREWS. The filter is a real field-replaceable assembly - the guide gives it a three-step procedure: loosen the cover's captive screws, swap the old filter for a new one, then refit the cover and tighten the captive screws - and the Overview numbers it as item 3. What is NOT resolvable is where one cover ends and the next begins: the mesh WINDOWS measure cleanly but a cover's own edge is a shadow line a pixel wide, and the screw heads sit in the top strip where the filter media's texture defeats every threshold that finds a smooth disc elsewhere on the face. The filters are therefore drawn as the vent fields they present rather than as seated FRU components. A mechanical drawing, or a straight-on photograph of the front at 5+ px/mm, would settle it.

THE FACEPLATE OF THE 48 VDC SUPPLY. The datasheet offers '48 VDC Power Supply: Input Voltage: 40 to 72 VDC' beside the AC one, but both staged documents draw and photograph only the AC machine - the guide's Overview calls out '8. 2 x AC PSUs' and both rear elevations show C14 inlets. There is no DC face to model, so no cor550-psu-dc part was written, and the dc-f2b configuration seats the AC part - wrong at the connector, which is what this gap and lint L120 keep in view until a DC face turns up.

THE VENDOR ORDERING CODES FOR THE AC SUPPLY AND THE FAN TRAY. The datasheet's ordering table lists chassis SKUs only (carried on the configurations), and the guide's replacement procedures name no part. Both FRUs are therefore named for the chassis, which library/components/README.md allows only because no model number exists to use instead. If a COR550 ordering table lands, both parts should be renamed to their FRUs and this device should take the major that costs - edgecore/fan-2u-1x1sn@1 is the precedent for both the rename and its price.

WHETHER EACH TRAY CARRIES ONE FAN OR TWO IN SERIES. The datasheet says '4+1 redundant, hot-swappable fan modules' and 'Fans: Hot-Swappable 4+1 redundant fans' and never gives a fan count. One rotor is visible through each tray's mesh. This vendor's other 2RU trays carry two in series and say so in words - edgecore/fan-2u-1x1sn@1's datasheets print '4 hot-swappable fan modules (2 fans per module), 8 fans total' - but nothing of the kind is printed for this machine, so the bay count is five and the fan count is not claimed.

devices.description: 4x 10G SFP+, 8x 1G SFP and 4x 1G RJ-45 fanless cell site gateway, sold as the CSR180, Broadcom BCM88273 Qumran-UX with an Intel Atom C3308 and a Stratum 3E OCXO. The CSR200's shell with no fans in it: passively cooled behind a honeycombed faceplate, needing at least 1 m/s of external airflow, with no FAN lamp and no BITS port. Ports number from 1; all timing, management and power connections are on the front, and the two DC supplies are fixed.

gaps.wanted: A figure or drawing of this faceplate that can carry a dimension. THE ONE THAT EXISTS CANNOT, AND THE PROOF IS A STANDARD IT CONTRADICTS. Its SFP cage pitch reads 14.7-14.75 measured two ways - across the four cage bores and across the shell walls between them - against the SFF-8432 figure of 14.25 that the registry carries and that the CSR200's figure reproduces at 14.22. Its RJ-45 cell pitch reads 14.4 against a registry 13.97, the same three percent high. And its DC terminal blocks read about eleven percent SMALL against the sibling's. Nothing reconciles those with one scale. THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION WAS TESTED AND FAILED. A perspective render would taper: panel height sampled along x is flat on both faces, 425-419 px across the CSR200 and 425-430 across this one, and the CSR180's absolute feature POSITIONS line up with the CSR200's to a millimetre or two over the whole 440. What is wrong is local scale, not geometry - the art is honeycomb dark-on-dark at low contrast and repeated careful reads of one feature wobble by 0.5 to 1 mm where the CSR200's repeat to 0.05. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT: every standard part takes its size from the registry - SFP 14.25, RJ-45 13.97, USB-A, SMB - and the figure supplies POSITIONS and COUNTS only. That is the division docs/modelling-a-device.md already draws for ganged pitch, applied to the whole face. The two non-standard parts, common/dc-terminal-24@1 and edgecore/filter-slot-5915-16x@1, are sized from edge POSITIONS for the same reason, and each says so.

Which of the four stacked RJ-45 positions is which. The face carries two 1x2 stacks - four jacks - and the datasheet names only THREE non-traffic RJ-45s: the console (callout 4), the ToD/1PPS (callout 10) and the management port (callout 11). There is no BITS port on this model, which is the CSR200's callout 4 and the reason that device has twelve callouts and this one eleven. The silkscreen under the left stack is a single lamp and legend where the CSR200 has two, and it is not legible at 9.63 px/mm. So the fourth position is either blank or something unlisted, and the three that are named are placed here in the CSR200's order - console top right, management bottom right, ToD/1PPS bottom left - which is an INFERENCE FROM THE SIBLING, not a reading.

A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one. The quick start's step 3 does picture the grounding point - a two-hole lug on the SIDE panel near the rear, with the earth symbol beside it - which is more than the CSR200's quick start gives, but a three-quarter view of a corner fixes no coordinate, so the lug is not placed. The side panels matter more here than on any other device in this family: this box is cooled by air someone else moves across it.

An LED table. Neither document has one, and unlike the CSR200's quick start this one does not even state that the PSU lamps come up green. Five system lamps are legible - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, ALARM - and every lamp here carries `off` and one green `on`, borrowed from edgecore/csr200 where a quick-start sentence supports it. Borrowed, and said to be.
Which of each optical port's two bezel lamps is link and which is activity - the same silence as on the CSR200, from the same vendor, about the same bezel.

Whether an air filter is sold for this model at all. The CSR200's datasheet lists two filter accessories with part numbers; this one's ordering section lists the base model and nothing else, yet the faceplate carries a filter slot and callout 5 calls it "Filter Slot (Optional)". So the bay is real, the cover is drawn, and what goes in it is unnamed by the vendor.

devices.description: 6x 10G SFP+, 8x 1G SFP and 4x 1G RJ-45 compact cell site gateway, sold as the CSR200, Broadcom BCM88272 Qumran-UX with an Intel Atom C3308 and a Stratum 3E OCXO. Temperature hardened to -40 to 70 C in a 240 mm-deep 1RU shell, side-to-side airflow with an optional air filter, and built-in fixed DC supplies and fans rather than removable ones. Ports number from 1; all timing, management and power connections are on the front.

gaps.wanted: A figure or square-on photograph of any face but the front. Both staged documents draw the front only - the datasheet's page-2 elevation is the sole elevation in either - so the rear panel here is bare metal. The quick start places a grounding point "on the device's rear panel or side panel" and ships a grounding kit of a lug, two screws and two washers, but pictures neither panel, so the lug is not placed: its face is known to exist and its position is not known at all. Airflow is side-to-side, so the left and right panels carry the intake and exhaust and are the faces that matter most here.

An LED table. Neither document has one. Six system lamps are legible on the faceplate - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, FAN, ALARM - and the only colour either document states is in the quick start's step 5: "After power on, the PSU1/PSU2 LEDs should be on green". So every lamp on this device carries `off` and one green `on`, which is what is known, and the real vocabularies - what amber on DIAG means, what ALARM signals, whether LOC is a locator beacon - are unwritten rather than guessed. The same silence covers BITS, PPS, LINK and ACT.

Which of each port's two bezel lamps is link and which is activity. Every optical column carries four lamps - two pointing up to its top port, two pointing down to its bottom port - measured consistently across all seven columns of both blocks. Nothing in either document names them, so they are `led-port-N-1` and `led-port-N-2` in the order they are printed, left to right.

A picture of the air filter. Edgecore sells two accessories against the filter bay - F0OEC5627002Z, "Assembled module with filter installed", and F0OEC5627001Z, "Air filter frame for field replacement" - and NEITHER IS PICTURED. Only the slot cover that ships in the bay is drawn, so the bay accepts that cover alone. The filter's own face is a second module waiting on a source.

The maker and part number of the three-pole barrier terminal block. common/dc-terminal-27@1 was created for this device and measured off this device's own elevation - 28.0 x 15.2 on an 8.5 pole pitch, read twice because the face carries two of them - but no document names the bought-in part, and its depth is estimated outright because a front elevation fixes nothing behind the face.

A dimension for the four timing jacks. The quick start calls them SMB - "the 1-pulse-per- second (1PPS) in/out SMB ports" - which is what picks common/smb-jack@1 and its 7.0 mm nut. The elevation supports the CENTRES, which read on a 14.17 pitch, and not the envelope: what is bright in the art is the gold collar at about 3.4 mm, and the nut's flats are dark metal against a dark panel. So the pitch is measured and the part's own size is borrowed.

devices.description: 20x 10G SFP+, 4x 25G SFP28 and 3x 100G QSFP28 cell site router, sold as the CSR310, Broadcom BCM88470 Qumran-AX with an Intel Atom C3508 and a Stratum 3E OCXO. An integrated GNSS receiver behind an SMA antenna input, six RJ-45s carrying stacking, timing and management, and two of the QSFP28s usable for stacking a second unit. Everything is on the front, including both hot-swappable supplies and the fan tray; side-to-side airflow.

gaps.wanted: A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one, and on THIS device that is a smaller hole than usual: the datasheet's own "All ports and PSUs are accessible at the front" means the rear carries no user-facing hardware but the grounding point. The quick start's step 3 pictures that point twice, once on the rear panel and once on the side, as a two-hole lug with the earth symbol beside it - enough to know it exists on both, not enough to place either, so neither is placed. The SIDE panels carry the intake and exhaust on a side-to-side box and are drawn nowhere.

What the component at 239.8-260.8 is. It is 21.0 x 3.8 in the silkscreen band between the SFP+ numerals and the AS7315-27X model text, and it reads as eight cells with the outer two red and the inner six pale. Neither document mentions it: the fourteen callouts do not point at it, the specification lists no display and no switches, and the quick start's step 5 figure - which is otherwise the most legible thing in the corpus - is cropped just short of it. A stack-identity display would fit the device, which stacks two units and has a STACK-SYNC and a STACK-CTRL port; so would a DIP bank. It is drawn as a plain bezel with no claim about which, and `common/seven-segment-dual@1` was NOT used, because reaching for a part whose name asserts what the thing is would be the guess this gap exists to avoid.

The module letters on the two-high QSFP28 block at 322.5-342.5. The quick start names M0 (the single 100G cage) and M1 (the SFP28 group) outright, and the datasheet elevation carries a `M? 100GBASE-R` label over this block that does not resolve at 8.15 px/mm - it could be M2 or M3, and the block holds two ports whose own numbering is unread. They are modelled as `stack-0` and `stack-1` from the datasheet's callout 11, "2 x 100G QSFP28 stacking ports", which is a function rather than a name.

What the six lamps in the stacking block's bezel do. Their positions are measured - 325.1, 327.5, 330.4, 334.3, 337.5, 339.7 - and two of the six are visibly larger than the other four, which usually means a port lamp beside a set of lane lamps. Nothing in either document says. Four lane lamps and two port lamps is the shape the AGR110 uses, but that is a pattern, not a reading, so the six are placed and left unassigned.

How many fans are in the tray. The datasheet says "Hot swappable redundant fan modules" - plural, inside one tray - and the FRU table sells exactly one "Fan Tray Spare Part", FAN-1U-1x1J-S. The elevation shows a closed tray with no grille and no seams. So the tray is one module with no nested bays and the redundancy is stated in attrs without a count, rather than a number being invented to fill the field.

A wattage for either supply. The datasheet's "Power Capacity: 300 W (maximum)" and the quick start's "193 Watts maximum" are both the CHASSIS's - one a capacity, one a consumption - and neither is an output rating for a module. Input ranges are published for both variants and are carried on the parts; the output is not, so L27 stands on both and the hole stays visible.

An LED table. Neither document has one. Six system lamps are named on the faceplate - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, FAN, ALRM - and the quick start states one colour for four of them: "After power on, the PSU1/PSU2, DIAG, ALRM, and FAN LEDs should all be on green." That is more than the CSR200 gives and still not a vocabulary, so every lamp carries `off` and one green `on`.

devices.description: 20x 25G SFP28 and 4x 100G QSFP28 cell site router, sold as the CSR430, Broadcom BCM88284 Qumran-2U with an Intel Atom C3508 and 2 GB of GDDR6 deep buffer. An SMA GNSS antenna input, SMB 1PPS and 10 MHz jacks, a ToD RJ-45, and a rotated USB-A. Everything is on the front - ports, both hot-swappable supplies and the fan tray - with side-to-side airflow. Ports number 0-23 in one range, the four QSFP28s first.

gaps.wanted: A third statement. csr430-datasheet says "440 x 300 x 44 mm" and 5.44 kg; csr430-qsg's hardware specification says "438.4 x 300 x 43.7 mm" and 5.42 kg. Both are single-model documents for the AS7515-24X, so this is not a shared quick start describing a sibling. The datasheet is taken because the figure's measured aspect of 9.9091 sits nearer 10.0 than 10.0320, and because the CSR310 - which the programme records as sharing this shell - states 440 x 300 x 44 in BOTH its documents. That is three statements against one, and it is still a disagreement rather than a resolution.

A part number for this device's fan tray. The CSR430's datasheet carries no field-replacement table; its quick start describes replacing the tray without naming it. edgecore/csr310-fan-tray@1 is fitted here on the strength of the DRAWING ALONE - handle, AIRFLOW arrow and thumbscrew within about two millimetres on both elevations, which is the noise floor at 8-9 px/mm. The supplies are shared on much better evidence, a part number stated in this device's own quick start. This one is an identification, not a proof, and a part number would settle it either way.

A figure of any face but the front, which on this device is a smaller hole than usual and is worth saying why. The datasheet's key features include "All ports, PSUs and fan modules are front access" and "Maintenance activity to replace PSUs and FANs can be done from the front panel without remove the product from rack" - so the rear carries no user hardware at all. The quick start's callout 11 is a "Grounding screw"; it is not located, so it is not placed. The SIDE panels carry the intake and exhaust on a side-to-side box and no figure shows either. Per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md these faces are DECLARED empty with the reason rather than left silent, which is the difference between empty-by-verification and empty-by-omission.

What the white perforated strip between each QSFP28 cage pair is. On the SFP28 columns the equivalent strip carries one arrow lamp per port and three vent holes, and the quick start's LED table names the arrow lamps' colours. Between the QSFP cages the strip is a dense grid of rectangular openings with no arrows - it reads as a vent, and the QSFP ports' own lamps are the rectangles in the silkscreen band below, which is where the numerals put them. It is drawn as a vent on that reading; a photograph would confirm there is no lamp in it.

gaps.wanted: A picture of the DC supply's face. Both documents say the device takes "2 x DC or AC PSUs" and the datasheet publishes a DC input range of -44 to -60 V at 15.5-9.6 A per supply, so the variant certainly exists - but the only elevation draws AC modules, and the quick start's DC section pictures wiring and ring lugs rather than a module face. A way to print six different numbers from one contract. Each fan module's left-hand strip carries its bay number and a small airflow arrow - the rear elevation shows 1 to 6 at 17.1, 67.5, 117.3, 167.7, 217.0 and 267.4 - and they are printed ON THE MODULE, not on the chassis behind it. edgecore/csr440-fan@1 is one contract used six times, so it cannot carry six digits; drawing them as chassis silkscreen puts them under the module that covers them, which L21 correctly reports as printing on nothing. SO THEY ARE NOT DRAWN, and the numbering lives in the bay ids `fan-1` to `fan-6`, which is where a consumer reads it anyway. A configuration's `skins:` maps one skin per COMPONENT rather than per bay, so the fix is either six near-identical contracts or a per-bay skin the format does not have. One weight. The datasheet says "7.5 kg (NW) 16.53 lb"; the quick start says "6.8 kg (14.99 lb), with two installed PSUs". The dimensions agree to the digit between the two, so this is not two products - but the quick start is a TWO-MODEL document covering the AS7535-28XB and the AS7535-28XBE, which is the likeliest explanation and is not a reason to pick one. What the small white square beside the `Alarm` legend is. Between the QSFP cages the strip is a dense grid of rectangular openings with no arrows, and the two ports' lamps are the rectangles in the silkscreen band below, where the `Q-DD 1`/`QSFP28 1` legends put them. What is behind the perforated blank that fills the rear from 313.0 to the panel edge. Neither document calls it out - the rear elevation's only callout is 15, the fan modules - and it carries no handle, latch or fastener that would make it a module. It is drawn as what it appears to be: a vent field in fixed metal, with the grounding pad and earth symbol that sit on it. If it is a blank over an unpopulated bay, nothing here says so.

devices.description: 48x 10G SFP+ and 6x 100G QSFP28 data-centre leaf switch, sold as the DCS201, Broadcom Trident 3 with an Intel Atom C3558. All fifty-four ports, both management jacks, the console and the USB are on the FRONT; two supplies and five fan trays are on the rear. Ports number 1-54 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. Ships front-to-back and back-to-front, and the two builds differ in the colour of every handle and latch.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Neither staged document draws any of them flat: the quick start's mounting figures show the lid and one side in three-quarter view while brackets are being screwed on, which is enough to see that nothing is printed or punched there and not enough to model. Each of the four therefore carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md - EMPTY BY VERIFICATION, not by omission. L45 STILL WARNS ABOUT THEM AND THIS GAP IS WHAT ANSWERS IT, because that rule exempts a view a gap names rather than one carrying an `empty:` sentence. Worth saying plainly: the CSR440 clears the same rule only because an unrelated chassis-weight gap happens to scope all six views, which the rule's own comment calls over-exemption; this one names the four faces because they are what it is about. IT DOES NOT COST THE DEVICE ITS CAPABILITY LEVEL. I asserted that it did and was wrong - the grader reads six views here and the 3D build is whole. A mechanical drawing would still improve these four faces from honest blanks to drawn ones.

What the last two white legend boxes say. The label strip carries six bracketed groups of four - the breakout lane legend, one bracket per QSFP28 port, and they read 49 to 54 in order - and then TWO MORE boxes of the same size and pitch at 362.98 and 369.01 mm, under the numerals for ports 47 and 48, belonging to no bracket. At 5 px/mm their contents are not legible and no table in either document accounts for a seventh pair. They are left undrawn rather than guessed, and this gap is the record that they exist and where.

An orthographic elevation, or a mechanical drawing. The only full-panel figures this corpus holds are perspective renders: the top cover is drawn above the face and the face tapers 0.9% from its top edge to its bottom. That costs the vertical axis entirely - every y on both faces is constructed from the registry's row pitch and the family's idiom rather than read - and it leaves the horizontal axis with a 0.84% residual against the stated width, which is why the panel is 442.5 because two documents say so rather than because the drawing shows it. A flat elevation would settle the row positions, the label-strip height and the width residual in one pass.

A way to print a numeral and its direction arrow together. Each of the 48 SFP+ numerals is drawn on the metal as a digit followed by a small up or down triangle - "1 up", "2 down" - naming which row of the column the port is in. Block expansion generates the digit and has no vocabulary for the glyph beside it, and hand-writing 48 marks to add it would take the whole block out of generation for one triangle each. The digits are generated and the arrows are not; the row is unambiguous from the numeral's own side of the column centre, which is measured and correct.

The positions of the four QSFP28 breakout windows. The guide's Port LEDs table says each QSFP28 port shows "1-4 LEDs Amber (25G breakout)" and "1-4 LEDs Purple (10G breakout)", so there are four windows per cage, and the art at 5 px/mm shows a row of dots inside each cage's bezel band without resolving where they sit. One lamp per port is drawn, carrying all four vocabularies as states - the same choice edgecore/as5912-54x made on the same cluster. Four windows at invented positions would be a claim about metal this figure cannot support.

An elevation of the DC supply. The rear elevation draws the AC pair; the DC variant appears only in the small three-quarter "DC Power" figure on page 2, which shows the green three-pole pluggable terminal and the bail handle clearly enough to know what is there and not clearly enough to measure it. edgecore/dcs201-psu-dc@1 therefore borrows its face size from the AC supply, which fills the same bay, and marks every element position estimated.

What each fan module prints beside its airflow diamond. Every one of the five carries a diamond mark in its upper right corner, and at 5 px/mm the characters next to it are not legible. The convention across this vendor is an F2B or B2F legend that follows the airflow variant, and that is what is drawn, from common/fan-module@1's field of the same name; the DCS201's own art neither confirms nor contradicts it.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Nothing in this corpus draws any of them flat - the mounting figures show the lid and one side in three-quarter view while brackets go on, which shows nothing is printed there and gives nothing to model. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md: empty by verification, not by omission.

The four breakout windows per QSFP-DD port, drawn. The Port LEDs enlargement resolves them - a vertical column of four round windows beside each cage - and the table names what they mean: "400G: 1 LED Blue; 200G Breakout: 1 LED White, 1-2 LEDs Green; 100G Breakout: 1-4 LEDs Green; 50G Breakout: 1 LED Cyan". One lamp per port is drawn instead, carrying all four vocabularies as states, which is what edgecore/as5912-54x and edgecore/dcs201 do on the same cluster. Drawing the real four would be 128 placements and 128 cutouts, and the enlargement fixes them relative to a cage rather than to the panel, so their absolute positions would still have to be constructed. This records that the simplification is a choice here and not a limit of the source.

A way to say that HALF THIS WALL FEEDS MORE POWER THAN THE OTHER HALF. The datasheet states the upper sixteen ports support up to 24 W per transceiver and the lower sixteen do not - a real, per-row electrical fact that decides which optics can go where. The model has no vocabulary for a per-row power budget on a port group: `attrs` on the group would claim it for all thirty-two, and splitting the block in two to carry two attrs would misdraw a wall whose sixteen columns are one continuous pitch. It is carried in the device's optics prose instead, where a reader will find it and a tool will not.

What the sixth system LED window is. The System LEDs enlargement shows six windows in a 3x2 grid and the guide's own list names five - Loc, Diag, PS1, PS2, Fan. The bottom-right window carries no legend in any figure or table in either document. It is drawn, given an id and named in a region as an unidentified indicator rather than omitted, because a mark on the metal that the model leaves out is worse than one it labels as unknown.

A reading of how far the two end vent fields actually reach. Their PATTERN was corrected here - they were drawn as honeycomb and the elevation plainly shows rectangular slots - but their extents, 1.20 to 4.80 and 433.00 to 437.20, are still the ones set by the pass that got the pattern wrong, and nothing in this change re-measures them. THAT IS NOT A SAFE ASSUMPTION, because the sibling moved. edgecore/dcs511 carried these same two decors and its own photograph put the left field at 1.0 to 3.6, 1.2 mm narrower, which is what had its Loc, PS1 and Fan legends printing over the vent. IT WAS ATTEMPTED AND IT FAILED. A darkness threshold on this elevation returns the seams between slots rather than the field, and scoring columns by vertical periodicity - which should find a slot field and ignore a seam - returns four columns at 5.31-6.10 mm on the left, which is not where the field visibly is. At 5.08 px/mm a 1.8 mm slot column is nine pixels and the anti-aliasing defeats both instruments. This device's photographs are 1.105 px/mm and are worse. A square-on shot at the DCS511's 2.19 px/mm or better would settle it in one pass.

An elevation of the DC supply. The rear elevation and both rear photographs draw the AC pair; the datasheet rates a -48 VDC variant at 1600 W and the package contents list a "DC power cable (included with DC PSUs only)", so it certainly exists. edgecore/dcs240-psu-dc@1 therefore borrows the AC module's measured face and marks its terminal estimated.

devices.description: 64 x 100G QSFP28 2RU top-of-rack or spine switch (vendor alias AS7816-64X, OZ series), Broadcom BCM56970 Tomahawk 2 with an Intel Xeon D-1518, ONIE-preloaded. Every port is on the front, in sixteen 2x2 ganged cages; two 850 W AC supplies sit in the rear's lower corners either side of four 3+1 fan trays, in either airflow direction. Port, fan and PSU numbering start at zero on this series.

gaps.wanted: THE ONE-BASED AS7816-64X-O SERIES IS NOT MODELLED, and the documents disagree about which numbering they draw. The ordering table sells two base models whose only stated difference is that the O prints ports, fans and supplies from one and the OZ from zero; it also offers the 48 V DC supply only in the O series. The datasheet's elevations are the O, the guide's front enlargement is the OZ, and the guide's rear prints fans 4..1 beside a front that says PSU 0. This device is the OZ and prints fans 3..0 on the datasheet's word. A second device, or a silkscreen that can vary by configuration, would carry the O; a photograph of a real OZ rear settles its fan legend.

WHERE THE LAMPS OF THE TWO INNER PORT ROWS ARE. The vendor states four lamps per port and the outer rows show them, four round lamps above the top row and below the bottom. The inner rows - the upper cages' bottom row and the lower cages' top row - show none in either document: the band between the cages carries only the numeral and arrow legend, and each cage's white belly strip carries six round features per column, which is neither four nor eight and matches the cage's own light-pipe and vent pattern. 32 ports' lamps are therefore not drawn. A close photograph of one column of a real unit would settle it.

WHETHER THE BACK-TO-FRONT BUILD'S FAN HANDLES ARE A DIFFERENT COLOUR. Both airflows are orderable (-F and -B) and every rear either document draws has red handles. Other Edgecore lines colour the reverse build blue, but a sibling family's convention is not evidence for this one, so both configurations draw red.

FRU CODES FOR THE FAN TRAY AND THE 850 W SUPPLY. The ordering table lists chassis SKUs only; the guide's replacement text names no part. Both FRUs are named for the chassis because no code exists to use instead.

devices.description: 32x 400G QSFP56-DD data-centre leaf switch on an Intel Xeon D-1713NTE with an AST2600 OpenBMC, sold as the DCS511. Every port, both consoles, the USB and a 1PPS timing input are on the FRONT; two supplies, SIX fan trays and the grounding screws are on the rear. BOTH RIGHT-HAND CAGES ARE MANAGEMENT PORTS, which is not what the quick start's callouts suggest. The datasheet lists them under "Management Ports on Port Side" - "1 x SFP+ 10G ASIC management" and "1 x SFP 1G CPU management" - and states "Switch Ports: 32 x QSFP56-DD 400 GbE", a count with no SFP in it. Neither cage carries traffic.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Nothing in this corpus draws any of them flat - the mounting figures show the lid and one side in three-quarter view while brackets go on, and the -FF photograph is a three-quarter of the front. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md: empty by verification, not by omission.

The four lamp windows per QSFP-DD port, drawn. This guide's table needs all four to say what it says - "4 x 25G Breakout: 1 LED Orange, 3 LEDs Green" describes a row of four, not one lamp with four meanings - and one lamp per port is drawn instead, carrying the seven modes as states coloured by each row's FIRST lamp. Drawing the real four would be 128 placements and 128 cutouts on a face that already carries 34 ports, and the enlargement fixes them relative to a cage rather than to the panel. edgecore/dcs240, edgecore/dcs201 and edgecore/as5912-54x all make the same simplification; this records that it is a choice and not a limit of the source.

The six fan-bay digits, the PS1/PS2 legends and the two airflow arrows, drawn. All of them are legible in the rear photograph and all were measured: the digits 6 to 1 are white blobs 3.65 mm tall centred at x 122.85, 171.25, 219.66, 268.07, 316.02 and 364.42, a 48.5 pitch that matches the bay wall exactly; "PS2" spans 69.41-75.81 and "PS1" 363.05-368.99, each under a small arrow at y 33.1-34.9. THEY ARE NOT DRAWN BECAUSE THE BAY WALL HAS NOWHERE TO PUT THEM. Each digit sits about 2.4 mm past its bay's right edge, and with six 48.5 mm trays on a 48.5 mm pitch the bays are edge to edge, so every digit would land inside the NEXT bay's box - silkscreen painted over a module, which is L21's case. The metal plainly has a rail there that this wall does not, and deciding whether the trays are narrower than 48.5 or the pitch wider than it needs a rear elevation with dimensions, which neither staged document has. "PS1" alone falls in the real 9 mm gap between fan-1 and psu-1 and could be drawn; it is held back so that the rear is not half-labelled. edgecore/csr440 has the same gap for the same reason.

An elevation of the DC supply. The rear photograph draws the AC pair; the datasheet rates a -48 VDC variant at 1600 W and the ordering table lists AS9737-32DB-O-48V-F and -48V-B, so it certainly exists. edgecore/dcs240-psu-dc@1 is seated here and it borrows the AC module's measured face with its terminal marked estimated.

devices.description: 64 x 400G QSFP56-DD 2RU spine switch on a Broadcom Tomahawk 4 with an Intel Xeon D-1548, sold as the DCS520 and stamped AS9736-64D. ALL PORTS ARE ON THE FRONT in TWO BANKS OF SIXTEEN STACKED COLUMNS, numbered from 1, with the legend `N (up)(down) N+1` printed BETWEEN the two cages of each column. Two 10G SFP+ management cages at the left are ports 65 and 66; five system lamps stand in a column above them; an RJ-45 console, an RJ-45 management jack and a USB Type-A stack at the right. SIXTEEN OF THE SIXTY-FOUR ARE 24 W PORTS and the datasheet names them one by one. It is the fourth device on the 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell and THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR WHOSE REAR PUTS A SUPPLY AT EACH END with the four fan trays between them - the AIS800-64D, the AIS800-64O and the AGR560 all stack two supplies at the left. One shell, two rear architectures.

gaps.wanted: A FAN FRU NUMBER FOR THIS MODEL. `edgecore/dcs520-fan@1` was written as its own part and it very probably is not one: the three other devices on this shell all seat a tray whose FRU number `FAN-2U-1x1SN-F` is printed in all three of their datasheets, and this machine's trays sit on a mean pitch of 85.58 against their uniform 85.71 - thirteen hundredths of a millimetre - with the same honeycomb, the same angled red bar with two pairs of slots and a central button, and the same corner lamp. THE MEASUREMENTS ARGUE FOR ONE PART MEASURED TWICE, NOT FOR TWO PARTS. The three gaps here run 85.54, 85.64 and 85.55, a spread of a tenth of a millimetre, where the other three chassis repeat 85.71 with no spread at all; and this face is 80.1 x 83.5 `measured` against the shared tray's 81.6 x 81.2 `photo-measured`, a disagreement of 1.5 x 2.3 mm. Irregular spacing and a face that misses by more than the pitch does are what pixel-measuring a drawing produces beside a dimensioned source. Two rulers, not two trays. NEITHER DCS520 DOCUMENT PRINTS A FAN PART NUMBER, so the argument that settled the other three is unavailable, and the drawings cannot settle it either: scaled to a common size and normalised, 46% of pixels differ by more than a standard deviation, but that is this guide drawing the tray bright with the rotor showing through the mesh against the AIS800 guides drawing it dark. A test that cannot tell a different part from different lighting decides nothing. One FRU list closes this. If it names `FAN-2U-1x1SN-F`, delete this component and seat the shared one.

WHERE THE RESET BUTTON IS. The datasheet's System and Port LEDs section ends with the bare line "Reset button", and neither document draws one that can be found: the guide's Overview callouts run 1-9 and none of them is a button, its System/Port LEDs enlargements cover the left end, the port field and the right cluster without showing one, and at 8.87 px/mm the datasheet photograph resolves the pinholes it does have - the grounding screws, the PSU status lamps - without any obvious candidate on the port side. So the device is modelled without it rather than with one guessed onto a plausible patch of metal. An enlargement of either end of the front panel closes this.

THE EXACT OFFSET OF THE LANE-LAMP STRIP FROM ITS CAGE. Four lamps per port is stated outright by the guide, the strip is visible on the posts in its enlargements, and its HEIGHT measures well - about 10.85 mm over four windows on a 3.5 mm pitch, which is why `common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1` fits it. Its x is the soft number: the enlargement puts the strip about 10.7 mm right of the column centre while the post it stands in spans 9.05 to 14.8, and the panel's two scales - 11.94 px/mm read across the columns against 10.53 read down the rows - do not agree well enough to choose inside that range. 11.0 is used and the render was checked against the reference at matched scale. A dimensioned faceplate drawing, or one enlargement with a known length in it, closes it.

devices.description: 24 x 1G RJ-45 PoE plus 6 x 1G/10G SFP+ 1RU access switch, sold as the EPS112 and stamped AS4625-30P. gaps.wanted: WHICH HEIGHT THE 440 x 350.3 x 44 SHELL IS ACTUALLY BUILT TO. Four instruments on this model's own documents - two of them exact to four decimal places - put its drawings at 440 x 44.00. WHETHER THE THREE FIXED FANS ARE ROUND OR RECTANGULAR. This model's guide and its rear photograph both draw round openings 25.1 across; the EPS121/EPS122 guide draws 25.5 x 15.9 rectangles at the same pitch on the same shell - 47.87 here against 47.8 there, and 25.1 across against 25.5. devices.description: 16 x 800G OSFP programmable 1RU switch on Xsight Labs X2 silicon with an Intel Xeon D-1713NTE, sold as the EXP800-16O. Every port, both the console and the management jack, the USB and a 1PPS timing input are on the FRONT; two AC supplies and SIX fan trays are on the rear. THE PORTS ARE NUMBERED FROM ZERO - the panel prints `0 (up) (down) 1`, `2 (up) (down) 3` and so on to 15, which is this line's only device that does not start at one.

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Nothing in this corpus draws any of them flat - the mounting figures show brackets going on in three-quarter view, and the -FF photograph is a three-quarter of the front. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.

The second lamp on each OSFP port. The System LEDs enlargement resolves FOUR triangles under each column - two up for the upper port and two down for the lower - and the guide names both: a left lamp carrying seven rate and breakout modes, and a right lamp carrying link, activity and a blinking red for "no link on one or more ports". One per port is drawn and it carries the LEFT lamp's vocabulary, because that is the one that says what the port is doing. Drawing both would be 32 placements and 32 cutouts, and edgecore/dcs240, edgecore/dcs201 and edgecore/as5912-54x all make the same simplification on the same kind of cluster.

One chassis size. The datasheet says 442 x 509 x 44 mm and the quick start's own hardware table says 438.4 x 589 x 43.1 - eighty millimetres of depth apart, with both self-consistent in inches, so neither is a typo. The datasheet's figures are used because the live vendor page agrees with them and because both of the guide's own elevations scale to a round 5 px/mm at 442 and to nothing in particular at 438.4. A DEPTH IS THE LEAST TESTABLE OF THE THREE and this model draws no side view, so nothing here would catch it if the guide is the right one. The weights disagree the same way, 10.005 kg against 13.48 kg with PSUs and fans installed.

Whether the 1PPS jack is an SMA or an SMB. A caliper on the real jack settles it in one measurement.

Whether a DC supply exists. The datasheet says only "AC PSUs: 1+1 redundancy, load-sharing, hot-swappable" and the quick start "2 x AC PSUs"; no DC variant is named anywhere, and no ordering table is staged for this model. The other Edgecore data-centre switches in this library all offer both, so its absence here is recorded rather than assumed either way. Only AC configurations are declared.

devices.description: The 14RU ANSI shelf of the Nokia 7360 ISAM FX (Lightspan Access Node FX) GPON/NGPON access node, part 3FE65209BA. Its line-termination (LT), network-termination (NT) and NT I/O cards stand VERTICALLY in one cage, left to right LT1 to LT8, NT A, NTIO, NT B, LT9 to LT16. datasheet.title: Oscilloquartz edgeSync+ OSA 5420 Series data sheet (Adtran, 2023)

devices.description: Compact 1RU PTP grandmaster, boundary clock, NTP server and GNSS receiver with a high-quality OCXO (Stratum 3 / G.812 Type III). Fanless. Everything is on the front: two hot-swappable AC or DC supplies, two expansion slots for timing fan-out cards, four 1G Ethernet ports (two of them combo RJ-45/SFP), BITS, ToD, clock and PPS I/O, and the GNSS antenna input.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives 443 wide and the manual 436 "without mounting brackets". Both of the face's own images measure 443 x 44 to about 1% and 436 x 44 to 2-3%, so the faces are drawn 443. The reconciliation - a front plate a little wider than the body - is read from one three-quarter render, not measured.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the chassis, or a ruler across a real unit's front and across its sides.

gaps.note: The product-page three-quarter render shows each flank with two fields of round vent holes and three pairs of screws, two of them the bracket positions the manual describes; it is at an angle that measures none of it. The top and bottom are shown by nothing. These four views carry the envelope only.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of one flank and of the lid.

gaps.note: Manual p46 - blank plates "must be installed in unused PSU or expansion slots", each with a captive thumbscrew on the right. No image of either blank is held. The expansion-slot blank is modelled from that text alone (oscilloquartz/osa542x-lc-blank@1, art estimated); the PSU blank is not modelled, so a pulled supply draws as its opening.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or drawing of the expansion-slot and PSU blank plates.

gaps.note: The IRIG-B card's optical output is a round barrel 7.4 across in a 375 px render; no document names the connector type.
gaps.wanted: the IRIG-B card's own data sheet or a newer install manual.

gaps.note: The manual gives part numbers for the BTOH-16, CPOH-16 and PTOH-16 and defers the PSUs, the GE-4S and everything else to the OSA 5420/5421 System Description, which is not held. The IRIG-B card postdates the manual.
gaps.wanted: the OSA 5420/5421 System Description.

So the front view draws no vent of its own and whether the chassis carries any is unresolved. RE-READ when the duplex adapters renamed their bores from tx and rx to fibre positions 1 and 2 (the adapter at v5, and the A22 that composes it, in the traffic slots at v2): the rename lives inside the slot occupants, not on the chassis front between them, so it neither closes this gap nor opens one - the gap stands.

gaps.note: These four views carry the ENVELOPE ONLY - the 440 x 45 x 500 box from the manual's spec table, with the front faceplate shown edge-on as a dark band - and no observed surface detail: no lid screws, no side rails, no ventilation. The populated three-quarter render (fig 1-1) does show the lid and the left flank, but it is a lit marketing render on a black ground at an angle that measures nothing.

devices.description: UfiSpace S9321-64EO 800G AI/ML data center switch - 2RU white box, 64x OSFP 200/400/800G in four rows of sixteen plus a stacked SFP28 management pair, 1PPS and 10MHz SMB timing inputs and an RJ45/micro-USB console, Broadcom Tomahawk 5 at 51.2 Tbps; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 3000W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable in AC or DC, front-to-back airflow only. The OSFP faceplate is what separates this from the S9321-64E, which is the same chassis with 64 QSFP-DD

gaps.note: spec/schemas/standards.yaml carries no `osfp` key, so std/osfp@1 - built for this device - declares `interface: osfp` instead of `conforms:`, and L9 therefore never checks its 23.10 x 13.50 mm aperture against anything. The number is measured off HIG Figure 8 and corroborated by the OSFP MSA module envelope (22.58 x 13.0 mm), which is not the same thing as the MSA's own faceplate-opening figure. The cage DEPTH, 47 mm, is a straight estimate: no held document dimensions an OSFP receptacle. The same absence shows up a second time in the tooling: lint's own PLUGGABLE_CAGES set lists eleven cage media and not osfp, so L40 skips the osfp-800g group and then reports `attrs.optics-osfp` as naming no group's media. The group carries 1g because two independent tables agree on it and the third source is a figure callout, which the source-role table ranks below a spec table for anything but arrangement. gaps.wanted: a higher-resolution rear photograph, or a rear mechanical drawing.

gaps.note: The two fixed supply feeds are real, distinguishable things - the HIG's PSU lamp table tells PSU1-good-PSU2-bad apart from PSU1-bad-PSU2-good - but they are not addressable in this manifest. A fixed supply seats nothing, so there is no bay; the six screw terminal posts are panel metal and are drawn as decor; and the library has no terminal block component to place over them. The PSU lamp therefore points at the chassis and the PSU 0 / PSU 1 legends are chassis silkscreen, which loses the per-feed link a consumer would want. gaps.note: Five screws are visible along the lower edge of the rear photograph on roughly a 100 mm pitch and are drawn there, but no figure dimensions them and the photograph resolves 0.27 mm per pixel only in x - its vertical is compressed by the drop shadow. devices.description: UfiSpace S9511-20CT disaggregated cell site gateway router - 1RU temperature-hardened white box, 20 interfaces in three colour-coded blocks: four 1G RJ45/SFP combo ports in brown, eight 1/10G SFP+ in blue and eight 1/10/25G SFP28 in olive, behind a Broadcom Qumran2n at 100 Gbps with a Stratum 3E OCXO, an internal GNSS receiver and GNSS, 1PPS, 10MHz, ToD and BITS timing interfaces. Both the dual-feed DC supply and the 3+1 fans are FIXED, so the chassis has no bays at all

gaps.note: HIG section 8 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR) and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The Port Overview draws an up/down green pair in the web of every optical column, so which port each lamp belongs to is clear from the arrows; what its colours and behaviours mean is not. Every port lamp therefore keeps common/led-dot's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Rows of the system-lamp tables are annotated 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than merely undocumented - a different fix, and the reason this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: THE FRONT PHOTOGRAPH IS NOT THE DOCUMENTED BUILD, and the matched-scale comparison is what found it. Both text sources describe one fixed supply - the datasheet's Redundancy row reads 'Dual-feed one power stage PSU' and the HIG's PSU Overview says 'Dual-feed one power stage fixed PSU' - and both HIG elevations draw two three-post screw terminal blocks under INPUT0 and INPUT1. The vendor's own front render instead shows, in the same 0-115 mm of faceplate, a REMOVABLE AC PSU: silver face, blue release latch, hex grille, black handle, green status lamp and a C14-family IEC inlet, in a bay with a vertical PSU legend beside it, and a second bay carrying a blank filler. Everything to the right of 115 mm is identical in both - the timing column, the lamp block, the stacked jacks and all three colour-coded port blocks with the same numbering - so this is the same product with a different power end, not a different product. The DC build is modelled because it is the one two documents describe and draw; the AC build is not, because no held source dimensions its bays, and guessing them from a 1.18 px/mm render would put invented bay geometry in the manifest.
gaps.wanted: an AC-version front elevation or a PSU module drawing, which would also settle whether the AC supply is 1+1 removable where the DC one is fixed

gaps.note: This chassis has no bays, so neither its two DC feeds nor its four fans is addressable. They are real, distinguishable things - the HIG's FAN lamp reports one or more fans failed, and the rear legends number them FAN0 to FAN3 - but a fixed part seats nothing, the terminal posts and the grilles are panel metal drawn as decor, and the library has no terminal-block or fan-grille component to place over them. The FAN and PWR lamps therefore point at the chassis. Recorded rather than papered over with groups nothing joins. This is the same shortfall the S9502-16SMT records for its fixed supply; that device needed a terminal block, this one needs a fan grille as well.
gaps.wanted: a terminal-block or power-inlet component and a fixed-fan-grille component that a non-removable part can be placed as

gaps.note: The five system lamps sit on a measured 2.545 mm centre pitch and the library's nearest part, common/led-rect@1, is 2.6 mm tall - taller than the pitch allows, so five of them placed as measured would overlap by 0.055 mm each and L13 would rightly reject it. The column is stretched to a 2.62 mm pitch and is 0.4 mm taller than the vendor prints it.
gaps.wanted: a ~4.6 x 2.4 mm indicator component, or a caliper on the lamp window

gaps.note: No held figure draws the top or bottom of this chassis - Figure 5's overview gives front and rear elevations only, unlike the S9500-22XST and S9502-16SMT guides which both include a dimensioned top view. The bottom face carries only the compliance sticker, also estimated.
gaps.wanted: a top view in a revised HIG, or a photograph of the lid

gaps.note: The S9600-30DX HIG has no LED table at all - not for the port lamps, not for the five front-panel system lamps, not for the PSU or fan FRUs. That is a stronger silence than the sibling guides', which table the system and FRU lamps and only omit the ports. Every lamp on this device therefore keeps its component's off/on default. The two lamps beside each QSFP28 pair and the one on each QSFP-DD light-pipe strip are drawn because the photograph and Figure 8 both show them; what they mean is not stated anywhere.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: Section 10 of this guide verifies system operation without a single LED table, so the six front-panel lamps (which the photograph shows as five green and one blue), the PSU lamp and the fan lamp have no published vocabulary. The S9500-30XS and S9510-28DC guides table theirs, and the temptation is to borrow: that is not done here, because those are different platforms and a borrowed table would read in the manifest exactly like a sourced one. The legend block's row order - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - is read off the artwork, not off a table.
gaps.wanted: a section 10 with LED tables in a later HIG revision, or a NOS state map

gaps.note: The HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 113 x 81.5 mm. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation puts two independent repeated features - the airflow tag and the status lamp - on an 84.4 mm pitch across the four modules, so the repeating unit is 84.4 and the visible face is that less a small web. The manifest carries an 82.5 mm face on an 84.4 mm pitch. This is the third UfiSpace fan in the library to show the same split, and the likely resolution is the same one: 81 measures the fan BODY behind a wider flange. That is an inference and neither document says it.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-803816, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: No held figure of the rear passes an aspect gate. HIG Figure 7 draws the chassis top surface in perspective above the rear face, so its bounding box measures 4.217 against a true 4.9715 and its vertical scale cannot be taken directly. The face was anchored instead on the PSU stack, whose 40 mm height the HIG states, which fixes the scale but not the origin better than about a millimetre. Every vertical number on the rear - the fan bay top and height, the PSU bay tops - therefore carries about ten times the uncertainty of the front, where the photograph passed the gate at 0.3%.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear elevation, or an orthographic rear photograph

gaps.note: The HIG has a whole section on replacing an air filter (Figure 42) and the filter is not modelled, because no held figure shows where it sits on a face. Figure 42 draws the filter being drawn out of the chassis in three-quarter view without establishing which face it enters, and the front and rear elevations show no filter frame. A part with a replacement procedure is a part, not decoration - so its absence here is a missing component and not a decision.
gaps.wanted: a figure or photograph locating the air filter's access on a face

gaps.note: The C20 identification for the AC supply's inlet rests on the drawn three-slot pattern in HIG Figure 7 and on the datasheet's 200-240 V 10 A input, not on a stated cord type: unlike the S9311-64D's guide, which names 'IEC60320 C19', this one never names the cord anywhere. A C19 cord and a C20 inlet are the natural reading at 1600 W, and the drawn aperture measures 19.6 x 36.5 against the registry's 24.4 x 32.4 rotated cutout, which is close but not exact.
gaps.wanted: a close-up photograph of the PSU-162 inlet, or a cord type in a later revision

gaps.note: No held figure shows a DC build seated in the chassis. HIG Figure 7 and every product render show the AC unit with its appliance inlet, and the guide's DC section illustrates cable routing rather than the faceplate, so the DC contract carries the AC unit's measured face with a two-post terminal block substituted on the inlet's footprint. The datasheet rates the DC input at -40 to -72 V and 50 A, which is a stud-and-lug interface rather than a coupler, but its geometry is inferred.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of a DC-configured S9600-30DX

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9600-30DX, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and one fan. The datasheet mentions 'an external TCAM option' and a memory range without naming SKUs for either. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so the configurations carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide, or the TCAM and memory option SKUs

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9600-32X Open Aggregation Router datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9600-32X open aggregation router - 2RU disaggregated white box on Broadcom Qumran2c with 2.4 Tbps of switching and 4 GB of deep buffer, carrying 32x QSFP28 40/100G in eight two-high stacked columns plus 4x SFP28 1/10/25G that break out from 100G port 0, and a full timing block (GNSS on SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMB, ToD on RJ45, Stratum 3E OCXO, SyncE, 1588v2 Class C and TSN); four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 1600W supplies (1+1) at the rear

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives NO table for the port lamps. The sixty-four lane lamps drawn here therefore keep ufispace/lane-led-quad@1's off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nothing states whether the four lamps above a cage are four lanes, or a link/activity pair per breakout, or something else; the component's own provenance reaches the same conclusion from a different platform's guide.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The four SFP28 ports have no lamp of their own. Eight lamp groups are drawn in each band and there are eight QSFP columns, so none is spare, and the guide never mentions an SFP28 indicator. What the faceplate does say is that the first QSFP column's two lamp rows are painted yellow and orange, continuous with the SFP28 legend band, where every other column's are green - and the guide says those four ports are the breakout of port 0. The natural reading is that port 0's four lane lamps are the four SFP28 ports' lamps in breakout mode. It is a reading and not a statement, so the lamps here are attached to port-0 and port-1 and the SFP28 group carries no indicator.
gaps.wanted: a NOS LED table naming the breakout lamps, or a photograph of a unit with the breakout enabled and one SFP28 port linked

gaps.note: Three UfiSpace chassis guides dimension the same fan SKU three ways. This one's Component Physical Information table says 'Fan (W x D x H) 3.21 x 4.8 x 3.19 in (81.5 x 122 x 81 mm)'; the S9600-30DX guide says 81 x 113 x 81.5 and the S9600-28DX guide 80 x 113 x 81.5. The library part is 82.5 x 81.5, measured off a rear elevation, and my own elevation independently puts the repeating unit at 84.42 mm - face plus web - which supports it. The spread across the four numbers is 2.5 mm on width and 0.5 on height, under a pixel and a half at this figure's 2.96 px/mm, so no amount of re-measuring these figures resolves it. Reused rather than duplicated; the depth disagreement (122 against 113) is larger and is not measurable from any elevation at all.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-803816-HI, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: ufispace/psu-162-dc@1 records that no held figure showed a DC unit seated in a chassis, and built its face from the AC unit's with a terminal block on the inlet's footprint - grille left, connector right. This device's intake HAS such a figure: the vendor rear product render (photos/s9600-32x-3-view) shows two DC supplies with two-hole lug pads behind a cover, and their whole face is MIRRORED relative to Figure 7's AC unit - connector on the left, grille and lamp and bail on the right. So the DC face is probably not the AC face with a substitution, and the existing component draws it the wrong way round. The component is not edited from here; the render is 520 px wide and is evidence of arrangement, not of geometry.
gaps.wanted: an orthographic rear elevation or a close-up photograph of a DC-configured S9600-32X, good enough to dimension the terminal block

gaps.note: The panel numbers its ports inside the eight white lozenges in each lamp band, and at the best resolution the intake holds those numerals are two pixels tall and cannot be read. The numbers printed here are the column assignment the module-face numerals give, placed at the measured lozenge positions - the positions are measured and the digits are inferred. If the lozenges turn out to carry something else (a lane letter, a pair label), the positions stay right and the text is wrong.
gaps.wanted: a high-resolution front photograph, or a dimensioned faceplate drawing

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number. The datasheet names the product only as S9600-32X and its Available to Order block names only the two PSUs (PSU-162-DESR, PSU-162-AESR) and the one fan (FAN-803816-HI); the HIG prints no number anywhere. The S9510-28DC precedent applies - that model's SKUs came from the owner and from no held PDF - so the configurations here carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide

gaps.note: At the junction between the yellow SFP28 legend band and the green QSFP28 band the faceplate prints a black up-triangle on the yellow and a white down-triangle on an orange strip, and the orange strip runs under the first column's lower lamp row. Both bands and both markers are drawn here because they are on the metal. Neither document explains the colour coding or the two triangles beyond the Port Overview sentence about the breakout, so what the orange specifically marks - the disabled port, the shared lanes, the lower row - is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a legend or key for the faceplate colour coding

datasheet.title: UfiSpace S9600-56DX 100G/400G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet

devices.description: UfiSpace S9600-56DX 100G/400G open disaggregated aggregation router - 2RU white box on Broadcom Qumran2c at 4.8 Tbps with an 8 GB deep buffer, 48x QSFP28 40/100G in two blocks of six four-high columns, 8x QSFP-DD 100/400G with 400ZR/OpenZR+ in the middle, and 4x SFP28 1/10/25G that share in-band with QSFP28 port 0; a full timing block (GNSS on SMA, 10MHz and 1PPS on SMB, ToD on RJ45) with a Stratum 3E OCXO, an internal GNSS receiver and Class C 1588v2; four hot-swap fans (3+1) and dual 2000 W PSUs (1+1) at the rear, orderable AC or DC, exhaust airflow

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Each QSFP28 port carries a four-lamp cluster in the printed band above or below its block and each QSFP-DD port a lamp in one of the four blue light-pipe strips; nothing states what any of them means, nor - for the QSFP-DD strips - which of a strip's two lamps serves which of the two ports on that row. The lamp-to-port pairing written here is derived from the count alone (eight lamps, eight ports, taken left to right) and is the one thing in this device's LED model that is not read off a source. Every lamp keeps the component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with known ports up, down and passing traffic

gaps.note: The two lamps in the out-of-band jack's aperture are drawn green in HIG Figure 8 and are modelled, but THIS guide tables them nowhere. The link/activity vocabulary they carry is borrowed from the S9510-28DC and S9311-64D hardware guides, whose Management Port LED tables give 1G green on the left and 10M/100M amber on the right for the same class of jack on the same vendor's boxes. That is an inference from a sibling document and is recorded as one rather than being left to look sourced.
gaps.wanted: a management-port LED table in a later revision of this guide

gaps.note: HIG Figure 8 prints every port numeral on the schematic module face, where a seated transceiver would cover it, and the datasheet's product render of the same panel with the cages empty shows no numeral anywhere on the metal at 7x. The NUMBERING is certain and is used throughout; where the vendor actually prints it - on the bezel frame, on the EMI strip, or nowhere at all - is not established, so no numerals are drawn.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on high-resolution photograph of the faceplate with the cages empty

gaps.note: Same measure, same scope, two values, so it is filed rather than reconciled. The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the PSU 321 mm deep; HIG Figures 5 and 6, the vendor's own mechanical drawings of the AC and DC units, both dimension the body at 360.0 mm and 369.8 mm over the handle. Nothing in this model depends on it - a module's `size` is its face - but a rack depth budget would.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace PSU-202 datasheet, or a revision of the HIG that reconciles its own table

gaps.note: FAN-803816-HI is ordered by both this router and the S9600-28DX and the two guides dimension it differently: the S9600-28DX HIG gives 80 x 113 x 81.5 mm and this one gives 80 x 122 x 80 mm for the same part number. Width agrees; depth differs by 9 mm and face height by 1.5 mm. The component carries the 28DX figures because that is where it was built and where its art was measured, and this device reuses it unchanged rather than forking a second contract off a one-line table difference.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FRU datasheet for FAN-803816-HI

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the grounding location 'is covered with a protective label' and step 5 says to remove it, but neither the rear elevation nor the rear product photograph shows a label there - both draw a bare silver two-hole plate. The plate is modelled as the two images show it. Whether the shipped unit has a label over it, and what colour, is not established here.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of an unopened unit's rear panel

gaps.note: No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document. The datasheet's Available to Order block lists the PSU and fan SKUs only, and the HIG names the product S9600-56DX in its title, its overview and its dimensions table without printing a number. The configurations here therefore carry no `part-numbers`. The S9510-28DC's history is the warning: 'no SKU exists' was written there on exactly this evidence and was false, so this says only that we hold no document naming one.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or price list for the S9600 aggregation line

devices.description: UfiSpace S9600-64X Open Aggregation Router - 2RU, 64x QSFP28 40/100G in eight 2x4 ganged blocks plus a 4x SFP28 1/10/25G quad that breaks out of QSFP28 port 0, full timing (GNSS/1PPS/10MHz/ToD) on a Stratum 3E OCXO, four hot-swap fans and two hot-swap 1600 W supplies at the rear, front-to-back airflow

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the six front-panel system lamps, the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. Every QSFP28 column carries a four-dot cluster above and below it and the SFP quad carries the same, but whether those four dots are four lanes, or link and activity for two ports, or something a NOS defines, is nowhere stated. The sixty-four lane-led-quad placements therefore keep the component's off/on default. The datasheet's own footnote - "NOS integration is necessary to activate the specific feature" - is about timing, not lamps, so it does not even license calling this nos-dependent. Re-read 2026-09-18 when the fitted dc-populated configuration was removed - the library ships its models bare by policy (docs/pluggables-design.md decision 2) - and this gap is unaffected by that change.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The sixty-four numerals drawn on the port badges are placed from a measured badge position and numbered from the guide's annotation of the apertures - not read off the badges, which at fig-0015's 3.0 px/mm are two pixels of grey per digit. So the geometry is measured and the VALUES are inferred: what nobody has verified is that the badge over a column prints the same two numbers the guide writes inside that column's apertures. Every internal consistency check that can be run does pass - sixteen badges per band, two bulges each, one column each, and a numbering that closes at 63 - which is why they are drawn rather than left off. A single legible photograph of one block settles it.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the front panel at 600 px per block or better, or a vendor mechanical drawing of the faceplate artwork

gaps.note: One orderable part number, FAN-803816-HI, dimensioned three different ways by three UfiSpace hardware guides. This device's Component Physical Information table says 81.5 x 122 x 81 mm (W x D x H); the S9600-30DX guide says 81 x 113 x 81.5, and ufispace/fan-803816@1 was built from it at a face of 82.5 x 81.5; the S9600-28DX guide says 80 x 113 x 81.5, and ufispace/fan-803816-hi@1 was built from it at 80 x 81.5. The depth alone varies by 9 mm, which is not a rounding. Measured on THIS device's rear elevation the bay pitch is 83.87 mm and the module 80.9 mm high, which supports this guide's 81 for the height and is silent about the other two axes. fan-803816-hi@1 is seated here because its name matches the SKU; the bay is authored 81.5 x 81.5 so the sibling also fits. No third component was minted for a part that already has two.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the fan module's own label, or calipers on a real FAN-803816-HI

gaps.note: Neither document names an orderable number for the chassis. The datasheet's "Available to Order" block lists only the FRUs - PSU-162-DESR, PSU-162-AESR and FAN-803816-HI - and the HIG names the product "S9600-64X" in its title, its overview and its dimensions table and prints no SKU anywhere. Searched both documents for the string 'S9600-64X-' and for any hyphenated suffix pattern; nothing. The AC and DC builds are listed as configurations without part numbers rather than invented, and note that the sibling S9510-28DC's SKUs (-BN0B / -BR1B) came from the owner and not from any PDF we hold, so a suffix guessed from that pattern would be a fabrication.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quotation naming the chassis SKUs

Every watt figure in either document belongs to the box (565 typical, 1140 DC max, 1160.2 AC max), to a supply nameplate (1600, and the 1000-each 110 V derating) or to the provisioning reserve (1600 per circuit). gaps.note: THE 64 SFP28 LAMPS ARE THE TRIANGLES IN THE YELLOW BAND, and this gap used to say they did not exist. It said the hardware almost certainly had them, that HIG Figure 8's pale strip UNDER each module resolved to about two pixels at 9.585 px/mm, and that rather than invent 128 positions no reading supported, none were drawn. The search was in the wrong place: the lamps are above the modules, not below them, and the drawing already carried them - as 32 silkscreen marks reading `▲▼`, one per port pair, printed on the band. An up triangle for the top-row port and a down triangle for the bottom, which is the idiom the sibling S8901-54XC models correctly with common/led-arrow. Measured off the same figure, from the dark ink inside the yellow band rather than from a green cast beside it: each triangle is 2.35 x 1.47 mm, the two of a pair sit 2.79 mm apart, and the pairs repeat on a 14.37 mm pitch which is the port pitch.
